properties.decision:
Raised 2026-10-01 while planning cap:a-remote-client-signs-in-to-its-server-with-oauth-2-1. On flo2.io (Clerk, DCR off), a client with no pre-registration is known by a Client ID Metadata Document. That is an https URL serving a small JSON document whose `client_id` is the URL itself (draft-ietf-oauth-client-id-metadata-document-02). THE URL IS THE CLIENT'S IDENTITY: every consent a person gives is to it, and moving it later means everyone consents again.

WHERE IT COULD LIVE:
(a) A raw file in the reflow2 GitHub repository, as rust-sdk does. Free, versioned with the code. Against: a raw.githubusercontent path breaks if the repo or default branch is renamed.
(b) GitHub Pages for the reflow2 repo (https://sligara7.github.io/reflow2/oauth/client.json). Free, a stable https origin. Against: it is tied to the GitHub account name.
(c) flo2.io (https://flo2.io/oauth/reflow2-client.json). Already a domain Anthony controls. Against: it ties reflow2's identity to one host, and other servers (a team's Keycloak) would show "flo2.io" on the consent screen.
(d) A domain of reflow2's own. The cleanest identity. Against: it costs money and needs hosting.

WHICH REDIRECTS IT LISTS: http://127.0.0.1/callback and http://[::1]/callback, port-less. OAuth 2.1 -16 §8.4.2 calls `localhost` NOT RECOMMENDED and requires an authorization server to allow any port on a loopback IP. Claude Code's document lists localhost and 127.0.0.1, port-less, and signs in to flo2.io. Whether Clerk honours any port is measured in increment 0 before this is built on.

LEAN: (b), unless Anthony wants a reflow2 domain now. 127.0.0.1 and [::1] only, no `localhost`. A pre-registered client_id (increment 7) covers servers that do not take CIMD.
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-13 — reflow2's OAuth client identity lives on a domain reflow2 controls by DNS, not on a GitHub account path or on flo2.io
